rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Good day, stranger. You are at the city gate.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: No, stranger. Keep clear of the gate.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: That is not a question for the gate. Keep to your business, stranger.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: You need a reason to enter, stranger. I have no advice for you.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: The weather is no concern of mine, stranger. Keep to the matter at hand.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust is not required, stranger. Keep your doubts to yourself and your conduct orderly.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Good day. New, are you? Then you'll have to look around and decide for yourself.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: A hand? Nothing I can put you to just now. I'm on patrol, and the captain likes his guards where he left them.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Captain's the captain. Best not make a public sport of judging him, eh?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Advice? Keep your answers straight when the captain asks. Anything else, I’d only be guessing.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Aye, fair weather makes the west road look almost inviting. Almost.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You shouldn't, not on my word alone. Judge me by whether I do the job straight.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: New here, are you? Then keep moving along the east approach. I’ve nothing to tell you.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: A hand? No. Keep to your own business and stay clear of my patrol.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: What I make of him is no concern of yours. Keep to your business.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: You need to get into the city. Then take it up at the gate; I’ve no advice for you.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Weather's weather. Keep moving.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You shouldn't. Keep your distance and answer plainly.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Good day, love. You've landed in the inn yard; I'm Hessa, keeping the place moving.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: That’s kind of you, love. I’ve got the yard in hand just now, but it’s good to see an honest face.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Oh, love, Captain Roderic? Stiff as a fence post, but fair. That's what I make of him.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Ah, love, I wish I had some advice for you, but I can't tell you anything useful about getting in.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: It is, love—makes the yard feel almost cheerful, even with all the work waiting.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: That's your choice, love. I won't ask you to trust me on a word; judge me by what I do.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: New here, are you? I’m working. Don’t stand in the way.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Keep your hands clear of my stock. I’ve got work to finish.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Captain's not my concern. I have work to finish.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Then ask someone who knows the way in. I’m busy with iron.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Weather won't finish this order. Keep clear of the work.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You shouldn't. I don't know you, and I'm busy with the work.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Oh, good day! I’m Jory, and this is the smithy—I’m helping at the forge. You’re new, then?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: A hand? Well, there’s always something to do at a forge, isn’t there—but I’m only meant to handle scrap, so I’d better not put you to work on anything else. What can you do?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: The captain? I haven't got a thought on him yet, not one worth saying—and now you've put me wondering what he's like.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Into the city? I don't know anything about getting in, I'm only minding the forge—and I ought to be watching the scrap, but how are you planning to go?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: It is, and the forge feels less close in weather like this. Makes you want to be anywhere but sweeping, doesn't it?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust me? I haven't given you any reason yet, have I? I'm only helping at the forge, and I can keep to the scrap if that's what you need.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: A carpenter's yard. I’m Tomas, and I’m working.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: A hand would be useful, but I’ve nothing to set you to just now.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: A captain ought to know when a beam needs lifting carefully. Beyond that, I’ve no measure of the man.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: The gate’s not mine to open, and I’ve no advice worth giving. I’ve work to finish here.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Aye. Makes a change from rain while I'm working.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You needn't. I won't ask you to trust me.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Good day, friend. A new face is a small risk, but perhaps there’s value in knowing one another.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: A hand, friend? Perhaps—but first tell me what sort of work you reckon is worth your time.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: That depends, friend. What value do you put on a captain’s word?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: A city gate is a matter of value and risk, friend. What sort of bargain do you bring to it?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: A fair day for trade, friend. What brings you to my wagon?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust is a wager, friend. You needn't make it unless the odds suit you.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: New here. I heard you. I’m watching the south road.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: No. Keep clear of the road; I’m watching it.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: That’s not for me to judge. I watch the road and report what I see.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: I watch the road. The captain decides who enters the city.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Clear skies. I can see the south road.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You needn't. I watch the road and report what I see.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: New, are you? Hnh.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: No. Keep moving.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Captain's business.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Advice? Hmph. Ask someone else.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Hmph. So it is.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You shouldn't.
